intended_use: Generic comfort-oriented, reduced-graphic patient/family orientation display profile

source_attribution.creator: Human Reference Atlas (HRA)
source_attribution.attribution_text: Human Reference Atlas (HRA), "Brain, Male," version 1.01, NIH 3D entry 3DPX-020960, https://3d.nih.gov/entries/20960?version=1.01, licensed CC BY 4.0. Source data informed by Ding et al. (2016), the Allen human brain reference atlas, and the Visible Human Project.
source_attribution.change_notice: Modified from the HRA source: selected only external orientation structures; recentered, joined by anatomical region, decimated, smoothed, and recolored with high-roughness pastel materials. Deep structures, ventricles, vessels, pathology, blood, and cut surfaces are not included.

adaptation_contract.evidence_status: Design hypothesis only: muted pastel color and reduced visual density are not proven to be universally calming or anxiety-reducing; user testing is required.
adaptation_contract.recommended_trigger: Explicit viewer preference or a consented, clinician-governed application rule; never infer a clinical anxiety diagnosis from this asset.
adaptation_contract.information_policy: Reduce graphic detail and optional visual density; do not hide information that the clinician determines is material to informed consent.

assets.title: Comfort-oriented generic brain orientation
assets.description: External bilateral cortex, cerebellum, and brainstem in a matte pastel palette for low-detail spatial orientation.

warnings: Generic educational orientation only; not patient-specific.
Do not use for diagnosis, treatment planning, navigation, outcome prediction, or anxiety diagnosis.
Reduced graphic detail is not a substitute for informed-consent content selected by the clinical team.
The muted pastel palette is a comfort-oriented design hypothesis, not a proven anxiety-reducing intervention; test it with representative users.
The host experience must not use pupil, gaze, movement, or other biometric signals to infer anxiety through this profile; use an explicit preference or a clearly labelled simulated demo.
